name: ASIMOV Benchmark v1 + generated robot constitutions
modality: VLM/LLM under test receives (a) image + candidate action instruction (ASIMOV-Multimodal), (b) text injury scenario + action (ASIMOV-Injury), (c) ethical dilemma text (ASIMOV-Dilemmas). Scored as binary desirable/undesirable classification accuracy against human-voted labels ('alignment rate'); also run in an adversarial prompting mode.
what_it_measures: Whether a VLM controlling a robot judges physical actions as safe/unsafe the way humans do (semantic safety), and how much auto-generated constitutions raise that alignment vs no-constitution and human-written constitutions.
size: Validation: ASIMOV-Multimodal auto 1,311 actions from 50 contexts (train 11,080 images), manual 159 actions from 59 contexts; ASIMOV-Injury 319 actions from 50 contexts (train 2,335,361 actions from 361,947 NEISS contexts); ASIMOV-Dilemmas 200 (auto) + 284 (SciFi) actions.
reported_metrics: Top alignment 84.3% averaged across normal and adversarial modes with generated constitutions; Gemini 1.5 Pro / GPT-4 Turbo ~90% on ASIMOV-Injury validation without constitutions; 100% alignment on RoboPAIR self-driving jailbreak scenarios with constitutions.
cost_evidence: Data generated automatically from RoboVQA frames, Imagen 3 edits and NEISS hospital injury reports; human voting for labels on validation sets; no robot hardware trials; no compute or labelling hours stated.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is human preference votes on desirability; benchmark is offline (no correlation with real robot incidents reported). Inter-rater agreement not quantified in the paper.
notes: Sindhwani is last author. CoRL 2025 per project page and speaker homepage. Project page https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v1/ also fetched.

name: ASIMOV-2.0 (Can AI Perceive Physical Danger and Intervene?)
modality: Foundation model receives text injury scenarios (ASIMOV-2.0-Injury), photorealistic generated videos of safe-to-unsafe transitions (ASIMOV-2.0-Video), or image + embodiment constraint text (ASIMOV-2.0-Constraints). Scored by accuracy on risk type, severity, intervention timing, and constraint-violation rate against consensus human labels.
what_it_measures: Whether frontier models can perceive latent physical danger, judge injury severity, decide when to intervene, and respect embodiment-specific constraints (payload, gripper geometry) supplied via system instructions; also evaluates a 'thinking about safety' post-training recipe.
size: 319 text injury scenarios; 287 generated videos; 164 image-constraint pairs (validation sets).
reported_metrics: Top models (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.1) 92.3% average accuracy on risk-type recognition but 87.7-88.7% on severity; video-vs-text accuracy gaps of 27% (Claude Opus 4.1) and 40% (GPT-5); constraint violation rates 38.6-75% across models; fine-tuned Gemini Robotics-ER achieves the lowest violation rate with 50% shorter reasoning traces.
cost_evidence: Generator-critic-refine pipeline using Gemini 2.5 Pro, Imagen and Veo 3; 5 human raters per instance; video items kept only if rater timestamp std dev < 1.0 s; constraint items require >= 80% rater consensus; no robot hardware.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is filtered human consensus; scenarios grounded in real NEISS hospital injury reports (~100 hospitals, ~500K injuries/year). No correlation with deployed-robot incident rates reported.
notes: Sindhwani last author. Speaker homepage lists it under CoRL 2026; an OpenReview entry (go44bcifFA) exists but could not be fetched, so venue not independently confirmed. Project page https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v2/ fetched.

name: SciFi-Benchmark
modality: LLM receives a pivotal decision situation extracted from science-fiction works and picks among candidate actions; scored as agreement with human-voted preferred answers, in normal and adversarial prompting modes.
what_it_measures: Alignment of LLM decisions with human values in robot/AI decision moments drawn from fiction, and the effect of auto-generated constitutions on alignment and jailbreak robustness.
size: 824 sci-fi works; 9,056 questions; 53,384 answers (LLM-introspection); plus a smaller human-labelled evaluation subset.
reported_metrics: Sci-fi character decisions 21.2% aligned with human values vs modern LLMs 79.4% (base) to 95.8% (with constitution); adversarial 23.3% to 92.3%; the generated constitutions also score among the top on ASIMOV.
cost_evidence: Dataset generated by LLM introspection; human voting on the evaluation subset; no hardware.
validity_evidence: Human-voted labels only; text-only thought experiments, no link to physical outcomes.
notes: v1 title was 'How Would AI-Powered Robots Behave in Science Fiction Literature?'. Not a robot evaluation; text-only value alignment. Project page https://scifi-benchmark.github.io/ fetched.

name: Predictive Red Teaming (RoboART)
modality: Visuomotor diffusion policy; its RGB observations are edited with Imagen 3 along language-specified environmental factors, a policy-specific embedding anomaly detector predicts success rate as 1 - anomaly rate; predictions are compared with real hardware success rates.
what_it_measures: Which off-nominal environmental conditions (lighting, background, distractors, table height) break an imitation-learned policy, predicted without running the robot, and how well those predictions match real deployment.
size: 12 off-nominal conditions; 2 diffusion policies of different architecture; 500+ hardware trials (20+ per factor).
reported_metrics: Average absolute gap between predicted and real success rate < 0.19 (0.1 on the project page); Spearman rank correlation 0.8 between predicted and real factor rankings; targeted data collection improves performance 2-7x in predicted-bad conditions and 2-5x in unseen conditions.
cost_evidence: 500+ real hardware trials for ground truth; generative image editing replaces hardware trials for prediction; compute not quantified.
validity_evidence: Direct validation: predicted vs real success rates on hardware (Spearman 0.8, mean gap < 0.19).
notes: CoRL 2025 per speaker homepage. Best sim-vs-real validation evidence among the speaker's evals. Project page https://predictive-red-team.github.io/ fetched.

name: Evaluating Gemini Robotics policies in a Veo world simulator
modality: VLA policy actions condition an action-conditioned, multi-view-consistent Veo video model; 8-second rollouts under nominal, OOD (background, distractors, novel objects) and safety-probe scenes are scored by human evaluators with binary success; sim scores compared with real ALOHA 2 evaluations.
what_it_measures: Whether a generative video world model can rank and score robot policies for nominal performance, OOD generalization and physical/semantic safety as well as real-world evaluation does.
size: 8 Gemini Robotics policy checkpoints; 5 bimanual tasks; 1600+ real-world evaluation episodes for validation.
reported_metrics: Strong linear correlation between predicted and real success rates for nominal tasks; Mean Maximum Rank Violation 0.06 for policy ranking; correlations remain strong for background/distractor shifts; safety failures discovered in the simulator were reproduced on the real robot.
cost_evidence: 1600+ real episodes used as ground truth; human raters score every episode; generative rollouts avoid hardware risk for safety probing; no hours or compute figures stated.
validity_evidence: Sim-vs-real correlation and rank consistency reported against 1600+ real trials; discovered safety failures replicated on hardware.
notes: Sindhwani is a listed author (team paper). Pearson coefficient value not captured from the HTML fetch; the 0.06 MMRV figure is. v2 January 2026.

name: ASIMOV-Agentic (Gemini Robotics 2: Safety Evaluations)
modality: Embodied-reasoning agent (system 2) receives images, constraints and instructions and must route: call the VLA tool, refuse, ask the human, or call robot_stop(). Six components: constraint following (text / pointing / bbox / tool-use), human proximity monitoring from stereo images (single frame and 5 s agentic windows), safety-message tool calling, VLA feasibility (one-step and ToolEmu-style emulated closed loop), instruction ambiguity, obfuscated gauge reading. Scored by classification accuracy, MAE in metres, FNR/FPR, task and step completion.
what_it_measures: Whether an agent orchestrating a VLA refuses unsafe tool calls, stops for nearby humans, shields the VLA from infeasible tasks, and asks for clarification under ambiguity; plus real humanoid safe-stop tests.
size: Hugging Face dataset google/asimov_agentic, 2.4 GB parquet across 7 components; per-component item counts not stated in the report.
reported_metrics: Text constraint classification >= 96% for all frontier models but higher variance for pointing/bbox/tool-use; human distance MAE 0.35-0.55 m, 1 m breach detection 79-93%; agentic monitoring: FPR < 5% comes with FNR > 40%, FNR 10-15% costs 15-25% unnecessary stops, no model in the ideal quadrant; safety-message handling 100% for ER 2, Claude Opus 4.8, GPT 5.5; feasibility accuracy 62.0% (no VLA awareness) to 95.8% (detailed developer instructions); Apollo 2 humanoid lab tests 99% human detection and 96% safe-pose transition.
cost_evidence: Sensorized human-approach data (head-mounted ZED stereo camera, Vive trackers); synthetic constraint data via Gemini Pro and Nano Banana with human annotation and low-agreement filtering; Gemini-based VLA confidence emulator used to avoid physical robots or physics simulators; real tests on Apptronik Apollo 2 in a garage setting.
validity_evidence: Human-annotated ground truth; real-world safe-stopping validation on a humanoid (99%/96%). Report explicitly says it does not evaluate the certified functional-safety stack.
notes: Dated 2026-07-29; Sindhwani, Majumdar, Jindal, Kalashnikov, Sermanet-era collaborators appear in the alphabetical contributor list. Benchmark released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/asimov_agentic (fetched; gated, CC-BY-4.0). No arXiv version found. Blog post https://deepmind.google/blog/gemini-robotics-2-brings-whole-body-intelligence-to-robots/ (30 July 2026) fetched.

name: Gemini Robotics tech report, safety section (ASIMOV evals)
modality: Gemini Robotics-ER evaluated on ASIMOV-Multimodal (image + action VQA) and ASIMOV-Injury (text) semantic-safety sets and on content-safety pointing queries; scored by alignment/rejection rates.
what_it_measures: Semantic action safety of the ER model before and after post-training on ASIMOV data, and refusal of bias-inducing pointing queries.
size: Not stated in the report (uses ASIMOV datasets, see sermanet2025asimov).
reported_metrics: 96% rejection of bias-inducing pointing queries vs 20% baseline; qualitative improvement in semantic safety after ASIMOV post-training.
validity_evidence: none stated beyond offline ASIMOV human labels.
notes: Sindhwani confirmed in author list. Safety is Section 5 of a capability report; evaluation content is secondary. Cite only for the 96% vs 20% figure and the layered safety approach.

name: Gemini Robotics 1.5 tech report: ASIMOV-2.0 + Auto-Red-Teaming (ART)
modality: Attacker / Target / AutoRater LLM triad: attacker generates prompt attacks, scene attacks (edited images) and environment attacks (moving obstacles during rollouts) against Gemini Robotics; AutoRater judges failures such as hallucinated pointing. Also reports ASIMOV-2.0 safety evaluation of GR-ER 1.5.
what_it_measures: Adversarial robustness of the robot foundation model to prompt, scene and environment attacks, and semantic safety on ASIMOV-2.0 (risk recognition, consequence understanding, intervention triggering, safety-constrained pointing).
size: Not stated (number of attacks not reported).
reported_metrics: Qualitative: GR-ER 1.5 improves over GR-ER on ASIMOV-2.0 and reaches state of the art on safety-constrained pointing with 'thinking about safety' fine-tuning; no attack success rates published. Orchestrator failure analysis: planning failures 25.5% to 9%.
validity_evidence: AutoRater said to 'reliably detect' hallucinations; no human validation of the AutoRater reported.
notes: Sindhwani confirmed in author list. ART is the group's only red-teaming protocol description; numbers are withheld, so cite for the protocol shape, not for evidence.

name: Unsupervised anomaly detection for self-flying delivery drones
modality: Flight logs (control inputs + sensor readings) of hybrid aerial delivery vehicles; robust regression fits nominal flight dynamics while discarding contaminated missions; anomalies scored against injected and real anomaly types (3-sigma thresholds, turbulence, equipment faults) by detection rate.
what_it_measures: Whether a runtime/offline monitor can flag abnormal missions in a real drone fleet without labelled failures, under heavy training-set contamination.
reported_metrics: High detection rates across anomaly types (exact figures not in abstract).
cost_evidence: Real fleet flight data at scale; no labelling required (unsupervised).
validity_evidence: Evaluated on real flight logs including real equipment anomalies.
notes: Pre-LLM runtime-monitoring evaluation; Sindhwani first author. IEEE Xplore page (document 9197074) did not render; research.google page verified. Adjacent rather than central.

name: Embodied AI with Two Arms: zero-shot learning, safety and modularity
modality: Language-instructed bimanual system (LLM planner, VLM perception, point-cloud grasping, real-time trajectory optimizer with compliant tracking) evaluated on sorting, bottle opening and trash disposal with humans in proximity.
what_it_measures: Task success of a modular zero-shot bimanual system and its safe operation near humans via constrained trajectory optimization and compliance.
notes: Safety-paper nomination at IROS 2024, but it is a system paper: the evaluation protocol is not a reusable safety benchmark. Included as adjacent only; do not cite as an eval.

name: Barkour agility benchmark
modality: Quadruped robot runs a physical obstacle course inspired by dog agility competitions; time-based scoring with penalties.
what_it_measures: Agility (speed and versatility) of legged-robot controllers and hardware on a standardized real course.
size: One obstacle course with diverse obstacles.
reported_metrics: Custom quadruped completes the course at about half the speed of a dog.
cost_evidence: Requires a physical course and repeated real robot runs; no figures stated.
notes: Not safety. Included only as evidence that the speaker has designed a physical real-world benchmark; useful for cost arguments about hardware evals.
